proposal.thesis: HPE's quarterly operating margin swung from -14.54% four quarters ago to +7.0% in the latest quarter (deep_fundamentals quality_ratios, trend 'improving'), and TTM free cash flow grew to $3.99B (+3628% vs the prior TTM; quarter ended 2026-04-30) -- a real operating inflection the market has not fully re-rated, with the stock still 18.2% below its 52-week high despite +73.1% 3-month momentum and a 4-quarter EPS beat streak (last surprise +48.0%, quarter ended 2026-04-30). The 'why now' is the FQ3 FY2026 print on 2026-09-03 (27 days out, inside this 40-day horizon): a 5th consecutive EPS beat with a held-or-extended >7% quarterly operating margin would confirm the turn is durable rather than a one-quarter blip. Recent direct commentary frames the same story -- HPE's NVIDIA alliance (Zacks/Yahoo, 2026-08-06) and its quantum partnerships (Simply Wall St, 2026-08-06) -- but I am underwriting the print and the margin data, not those headlines. Per concept_memory, I exited HPE on 2026-07-15 and it ran ~+20% further within 15 days on catalyst news -- a documented left-on-table exit lesson; this proposal corrects it by writing binding invalidators up front. Momentum_health reads healthy, the regime is supportive (SPY above its 200-DMA), and this is a new, third demand_driver for the book (hyperscaler_server_capex, distinct from BKR's energy and DXCM's healthcare), so it diversifies rather than stacks risk.
